newsitem.title: LEBANON: Mahathir gives Lebanon investment rating.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir gives Lebanon investment rating.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad gave Lebanon a vote of confidence on Wednesday, saying it offered promising investment opportunities at an acceptable level of risk.
Ending a three-day visit to the Middle Eastern country which is recovering from a 1975-90 civil war, Mahathir said its investment environment was sound and it should attract foreign investors.
"I think Lebanon is now a good place for investment...In the extent that we can foresee, Lebanon is a good risk," Mahathir told a news conference before flying to London.

"We are proposing that there should be a joint commission between the two countries at ministerial level. We also think that the business people should have a Lebanese-Malaysian business council," he said.

Five Malaysian companies signed a contract with Lebanon's biggest company Solidere during Mahathir's visit to buy 8,000 square metres of prime seafront in central Beirut for a $75 million tourism development.
Mahathir, who was accompanied by four government ministers and representatives of Malaysia's private sector, said a special area of interest for Malaysian companies was toll roads and motorways.
"We are interested in quite a number of things including toll ways, different areas in development and also in other privatised projects," he said.
Last week, the Lebanese government decided to establish a $350 million private toll road company to build a motorway to Syria and ringroads around Beirut at an estimated cost of $1.2 billion.

"Our companies are looking into this and they look into the structure of the corporation that will build the toll roads in order to find out whether we would be able to participate in it or find some other way for working together," Mahathir said.
The Malaysian premier said he also discussed the possibility of establishing a Malaysian car plant in Lebanon but no agreement had been reached.
"We have not agreed on anything yet. We talked loosely about it but there is no agreement," he said.

Malaysian car maker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional BHd (Proton) said in a statement in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday that it would sign an agreement with a Lebanese company to make Lebanon its 44th export market.
Mahathir advised foreign investors to look seriously into Lebanon's investment potential: "I think there is a great potential for them to come here," he said.
He said incentives for foreign investors in Lebanon were "well in place".

"I think businessmen must of course take into consideration the so-called country risk published by certain agencies. As far as I can see...although there are risks in many areas, I think Lebanon would be described as a good risk," he added.
